extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about what actions one should take to overcome sorrow and achieve the highest goal while wandering the earth.
Bhishma cites an ancient dialogue between Prahlada and the sage Ajagara as an example.
Prahlada observes a wandering Brahmin (Ajagara) who appears healthy, wise, and detached, and questions him about his wisdom and way of life.
Ajagara explains his philosophical outlook: he neither rejoices nor grieves seeing things arise, grow, decay, and perish without cause, understanding all activities follow their own nature.
Ajagara describes observing the inevitable death of all beings—in sea, on land, in air—and celestial bodies, leading him to peace and equanimity.
Ajagara describes his ascetic lifestyle: accepting whatever food, clothing, or shelter comes his way without craving or aversion, whether abundant or scarce.
Ajagara concludes by describing his adherence to the 'python vow'—a state of stillness, purity, and wisdom that is recognized by the wise but rejected by fools.

key_points: State of detachment and witness consciousness
Distinction between wise and foolish understanding
